name: Alexander Nix

summary.text: Alexander James Ashburner Nix was chief executive of Cambridge Analytica and a director of SCL Elections Ltd and related SCL companies. In July 2019 he consented to a U.S. Federal Trade Commission administrative order barring deceptive statements about data collection and requiring destruction of data gathered through the GSRApp, finalised in December 2019. In the UK, after a referral from the Information Commissioner's Office, he gave a disqualification undertaking to the Insolvency Service dated 14 September 2020 that bars him from acting as a company director for seven years from 5 October 2020 to 4 October 2026, for conduct while acting for SCL Elections Limited.

facts.claim: The Companies House register of disqualified directors records a disqualification undertaking by Alexander James Ashburner Nix dated 14 September 2020, running from 5 October 2020 to 4 October 2026, under section 7 of the Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986, for conduct while acting for SCL Elections Limited.
facts.quote: Disqualified for conduct while acting for: SCL ELECTIONS LIMITED

sources.title: Alexander James Ashburner NIX - Disqualification Details

facts.claim: The Insolvency Service said SCL Elections had repeatedly offered potentially unethical political services to prospective clients, including bribery or honey-trap stings, voter disengagement campaigns and anonymous dissemination of information, without saying whether any were delivered; Nix did not dispute causing or permitting the companies to market such services. Nix said he made no admission of wrongdoing and that the government did not contend he had breached any laws, and told Reuters he accepted the ban to avoid a lengthy and expensive court case.
facts.quote: I have made no admission of wrongdoing and importantly the Government did not seek to press that I had breached any laws.

facts.claim: The Information Commissioner's final letter to the DCMS Committee (2 October 2020) states that the ICO referred conduct concerns to the Insolvency Service and that Nix, a director of SCL Elections Ltd, was disqualified from acting as a director for seven years.
facts.quote: Mr Alexander Nix, a Director of SCL Elections Ltd, is now disqualified from acting as a director for a period of seven years

sources.title: Letter to Julian Knight MP, Chair of the DCMS Committee (ICO/O/ED/L/RTL/0181)

facts.claim: In July 2019 the FTC announced a settlement with Nix under which he consented to an administrative order barring false or deceptive statements about the extent and purposes of data collection and sharing and requiring deletion of personal information collected through the GSRApp; the Commission voted 5-0 in December 2019 to finalise the order.
facts.quote: voted 5-0 to finalize the order and send a response to the commenter

facts.claim: Nix was a director of six companies — SCL Elections, SCL Group Ltd, SCL Social Ltd, SCL Analytics Ltd, SCL Commercial Ltd and another — all of which entered compulsory liquidation in April 2019.
facts.quote: All six of Nix's companies entered into compulsory liquidation in April 2019.

openQuestions: The Insolvency Service's own September 2020 press release was not located on gov.uk; its findings are quoted here from Al Jazeera and LBC coverage of the statement.
The Companies House register shows the ban ending 4 October 2026; the live register should be checked for current status.
Nix's removal as CEO in March 2018 after Channel 4's undercover reporting was not researched here.
